item.title: Bangladesh ranks 84th in Global Hunger Index 2026
item.description:
Bangladesh has ranked 84th in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2026, with a score of 19.2, placing the country in the “moderate” hunger category.
The index assesses hunger and undernutrition using four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and under-five mortality.
Bangladesh ranked ahead of India and Pakistan but behind Nepal in the index, which assesses hunger and undernutrition across countries.
India ranked 100th with a score of 24.1 while Pakistan stood at 106th with a score of 25.5. Both countries fell into the “serious” hunger category, according to the report.
Nepal ranked 72nd with a score of 14.5, placing it in the “moderate” category.
A lower GHI score indicates a lower level of hunger, while rankings reflect countries’ relative positions among those included in the assessment.
The Global Hunger Index is published annually by Concern Worldwide, Welthungerhilfe and the Institute for International Law of Peace and Armed Conflict (IFHV) to track hunger and undernutrition worldwide.
The 2026 report warns that global hunger is rising again, with conflicts, climate shocks and economic crises threatening food security.
In Bangladesh, 8.2% of the population is undernourished, while 24% of children under five suffer from stunting, or low height for their age.
The report also shows that 12.9% of children under five suffer from wasting, or low weight for their height, while 3% of children die before reaching their fifth birthday.
Bangladesh has made progress in reducing child stunting over the past two decades.
The proportion of children under five affected by stunting fell from 54.9% in 2000 to 24% in the latest assessment, a reduction of 30.9% points.
Under the GHI classification, scores below 10 indicate low hunger, scores from 10 to 19.9 indicate moderate hunger, scores from 20 to 34.9 indicate serious hunger, scores from 35 to 49.9 indicate alarming hunger, and scores of 50 or above indicate extremely alarming hunger.
The Global Hunger Index is published annually by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe to measure and track hunger and undernutrition worldwide.
According to the index, a lower score indicates a lower level of hunger, while a country’s ranking depends on its position relative to other countries included in the assessment.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,181 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,181.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,077, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in the Khulna division with two deaths. At the district level, one casualty each was recorded in Dhaka, Khulna, Kushtia, and Bhola.
A total of 1,306 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 209,876.
During the same period, 86 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,926.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 186,583 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 178,869 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: PM calls Dhaka’s air pollution a matter of shame
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday urged people from all walks of life to come forward to protect the environment and forests, calling Dhaka’s persistent air pollution a matter of shame for the country.
Speaking at a meeting to review the progress and implementation of activities of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, he also stressed the need for greater public awareness and collective efforts to build a liveable Bangladesh for future generations.
The prime minister urged government officials to take initiatives beyond their assigned duties to protect the environment and forests.
The meeting, held at the ministry’s conference room, decided to identify and preserve the country’s mother trees within the next six months.
It also directed the authorities to ensure regular care of planted trees, monitor their survival through field visits, and explore ways to expand afforestation in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
Noting that people have limited access to places where they can spend time in nature, Tarique Rahman stressed the need to increase such spaces and encourage people to develop rooftop and school gardens, as well as gardens in different buildings.
He said public awareness is essential alongside government initiatives to protect the environment, adding that greater awareness will make the work easier.
The prime minister also stressed the need for separate public awareness plans to support the implementation of decisions and programmes for environmental and forest conservation.
Expressing concern over Dhaka’s air pollution, he said the capital has been ranking first or second among the world’s most polluted cities for many years.
“This is a matter of shame for the country. Everyone must take responsibility from their respective positions to change the situation,” Tarique Rahman said.
Addressing ministry officials, he said they have the capacity to do more than their assigned duties.
“Your capacity goes a little beyond the duties assigned to you,” the prime minister said, urging officials not to stop at performing their routine responsibilities but to make further efforts for the country and its people.
He said not everyone gets the opportunity to work for the country, and those in responsible positions should make the most of it.
“Allah has given us an opportunity to do something for this country and its people. You may work from nine to five [9am-5pm]. Nobody will say anything if you do nothing beyond that. But if the environment deteriorates, future generations will suffer, because your next generation will also live in this country,” Tarique Rahman said.
He said everyone needs to go beyond their formal responsibilities and contribute more to keeping the environment healthy.
Those seeking change, the prime minister added, should use their abilities and come forward.
Referring to the plan to plant 250 million trees, he said the entire population will benefit if the programme is implemented properly. Collective efforts, he added, could bring positive results for the people.
The meeting also decided that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change will take initiatives to make up for any shortfall if other ministries fail to meet their tree-planting targets.
Regular maintenance and monitoring of planted trees will also be ensured.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo, State Minister Shaikh Faridul Islam, Prime Minister’s Special Assistant Dr Md Saimum Parvez, acting Secretary Fahmida Khanom and senior officials attended the meeting.

item.title: Dengue claims 10 lives in a day, highest toll yet again
item.description:
Ten people died of dengue in Bangladesh in the 24 hours to Thursday morning, matching the highest single-day death toll from the mosquito-borne disease this year, while 1,943 new cases were reported.
The latest fatalities have raised the country’s dengue death toll to 331 this year, while the new cases have taken the total number of infections to 107,259, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the deaths, four were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation area, three in Dhaka North City Corporation area, two in Chittagong division and one was recorded in Dhaka division, it said.
Earlier, on October 6, the country recorded 10 dengue deaths.
Since January 1, hospitals across the country have admitted 107,259 dengue patients. Of them, 101,031 have recovered.

item.title: Govt plans AI-based cancer screening at upazila level
item.description:
The government plans to introduce artificial intelligence (AI)-based screening and testing for breast and cervical cancer at the upazila level to improve access to early detection for women, Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has said.
He made the remarks while addressing a workshop titled “National Health Protection Authority in Bangladesh: Design and Structural Aspects” as the chief guest at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka on Thursday. The Health Economics Unit of the Health Services Division organized the workshop.
Speaking about women's healthcare, the minister said steps must be taken to ensure that mothers and women do not face embarrassing situations or harassment during pregnancy. To this end, plans are underway to transform health centers into one-stop service centers.
He said the centers would offer AI-based screening and testing for breast and cervical cancer. The government plans to introduce these services at the upazila level in phases and at a low cost.
The initiative is intended to make screening and testing more accessible to women at the upazila level, potentially reducing the need to travel to distant hospitals and making the services more affordable. However, the actual benefits will depend on implementation, service availability and costs.
The minister said primary healthcare was being given the highest priority to bring health services to people's doorsteps. The government has drawn up extensive plans to ensure healthcare for the population, but implementing all the plans at once would be difficult.
He said initiatives were being taken to prioritize activities and introduce them gradually through pilot programs.
The minister also stressed the need to expedite implementation of the Health Protection Act and related activities. Necessary steps were being taken by reviewing and coordinating laws from different countries, he said, adding that special emphasis was being placed on health insurance.
Noting that people have to pay substantial amounts out of their own pockets to cover medical expenses, the minister said this placed them under considerable financial strain.
Calling for coordinated efforts with honesty and dedication to address longstanding irregularities and challenges in the health sector, he said the government was committed to gradually delivering improved and quality healthcare at every level across the country.
Director General of the Health Economics Unit Dr Md Enamul Haque and officials from various divisions of the ministry were present at the workshop.

item.title: India urges Russia, Ukraine to protect Black Sea shipping
item.description:
India has urged both Russia and Ukraine to ensure safe passage for commercial shipping through the Black Sea as attacks on merchant vessels put Indian seafarers at risk and threaten to disrupt vital food and energy supplies.
New Delhi says discussions with both sides are under way.
“The targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways must be restored at the earliest,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said last week.
India accounts for more than 12% of the global seafaring workforce, with 311,936 maritime professionals, according to a 2026 industry report. And attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Black Sea in recent months have highlighted the risks facing civilian crews.
The Turkish-owned MV Royad Mammadov, a cargo ship carrying grain from Ukraine, caught fire and sank following an attack on Monday, killing two crew members. The three Indian nationals aboard the vessel survived, but sustained injuries and were taken to Romania to receive medical treatment.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for launching the strike.
The Defense Ministry in Moscow separately said it had struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea but did not specifically identify the ships.
The Liberian-flagged oil tanker Aframax Rio was also recently attacked by unmanned vessels off Russia’s Black Sea coast near Sochi, according to Russian authorities. The vessel was carrying 23 Indians, but all of them were rescued.
Anil Wadhwa, a former Indian diplomat, said India’s proposal to halt attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea covered energy infrastructure, safe passage for grain and energy exports, and an end to strikes on merchant vessels.
“Securing an ironclad guarantee depends entirely on a broader cessation of hostilities between Russia and Ukraine in the maritime theater,” Wadhwa told DW.
India’s close relations with Russia and expanding engagement with Ukraine give New Delhi access to both sides, but do not guarantee either will honor a shipping arrangement.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has described India’s proposal for a possible ceasefire with Russia as the “broadest” of the four offers Kyiv has received.
Russia has not publicly endorsed a binding safe-passage deal proposed by India, despite welcoming New Delhi’s peace efforts.
Rajan Kumar of the Center for Russian and Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University said India could use its diplomatic leverage with Moscow to help bring the two sides towards an agreement.
“India could play a constructive role in facilitating dialogue between Russia and Ukraine, particularly on the issue of ensuring the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea,” Kumar told DW.
He argued that India should also work with other influential countries from the Global South, particularly China, Brazil and South Africa.
“A coordinated approach with these countries could enhance their collective diplomatic leverage and strengthen their capacity to persuade both parties to adopt mutually acceptable arrangements for maritime security,” said Kumar.
India’s initiative comes as US President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine over the weekend, although its scope and implementation mechanism remain unclear.
Harsh Pant, vice president of the New Delhi-based think tank Observer Research Foundation, said Trump’s intervention could help India’s efforts but might produce a narrower agreement that fails to address New Delhi’s wider concerns.
“The energy ceasefire could be an initial confidence-building measure, whereas a Black Sea shipping arrangement requires additional commitments on attacks against merchant vessels, ports, maritime routes and the security of commercial traffic,” Pant told DW.
“India need not compete with Washington for the public credit of mediation. It could instead press for the inclusion of broader maritime provisions in any US agreement.”
Wadhwa said the proposed energy truce could also benefit Indian seafarers if it secured safe passage for energy cargoes.
“Although Ukraine alleges that the Russians have already breached this so-called truce, there will be pressure on both sides to allow energy cargoes safe passage. India is bound to gain as far as its crews are concerned in such a scenario,” he said.
The disruption to Black Sea shipping also has other implications for India such as delays in shipments of key commodities and higher transport costs.
“A prolonged Black Sea disruption would elevate India’s import bill mainly via higher freight on Russian crude and constrained soft oil supplies, with the strongest near-term transmission to domestic edible oil prices and food inflation,” said Lekha Chakraborty, professor at the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy.

item.title: IMF tells Bangladesh to maintain tight monetary policy
item.description:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advised Bangladesh to keep monetary policy strict to curb inflation, fortify its vulnerable banking system, and boost tax collection as talks proceed regarding a fresh IMF-backed package.
"Maintaining a tight monetary stance in Bangladesh is essential to counter inflationary pressures, which climbed to 8% in September," stated Sonali Jain-Chandra, deputy director of the IMF’s Asia and Pacific Department, during a news conference on the regional economic outlook.
She noted that Bangladesh faces ongoing hurdles across fiscal, financial, and inflationary domains, demanding structural measures alongside monetary restraint.
The IMF official highlighted financial sector reinforcement and revenue generation as urgent goals, pointing out that Bangladesh's tax-to-GDP ratio has been declining and ranks among the lowest globally.
"Comprehensive measures are required on the revenue side. Mobilizing resources is crucial for funding development projects and strengthening the broader economy and banking system," she emphasized.
Jain-Chandra mentioned that the IMF has been in dialogue with Bangladeshi officials since the nation requested a new assistance plan in May, after choosing not to draw further funds under its prior agreement.
A mission from the IMF visited Bangladesh in July to evaluate proposed policy changes, which she noted align with recommendations from the Fund’s Article IV consultation conducted earlier this year.
An Article IV consultation represents the IMF’s periodic review of a nation's macroeconomic health and policy framework, generally providing guidance on monetary, fiscal, and structural adjustments to mitigate economic risks.
Negotiations have remained ongoing following the July mission, she added.
"We maintain active engagement with the authorities and remain committed to assisting Bangladesh as it implements these critical reforms," she remarked.
Bangladesh aims to tackle stubborn inflation, banking sector vulnerabilities, and weak tax collection through a new arrangement with the IMF, though specific terms and schedules for the proposed package were not revealed at the press event.

item.title: Experts call for mandatory warning labels on packaged foods
item.description:
Public health experts have called for mandatory warning labels on the front of food packages to help consumers make informed choices as consumption of ultra-processed foods increases the risk of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Bangladesh.
They urged the authorities to expedite the finalization of the draft Safe Food (Packaged Food Labelling) Regulations, 2026, which would introduce Front-of-Package Labelling (FOPL) to alert consumers to the health risks associated with foods high in salt, sugar and saturated fats.
The calls were made at a webinar titled “Front-of-Pack Warning Labels on Ultra-Processed Foods: Progress, Barriers, and the Way Forward,” organized by research and advocacy organization PROGGA (Knowledge for Progress) with support from the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI) on Thursday, marking World Food Day 2026.
The webinar highlighted the growing consumption of ultra-processed foods containing excessive amounts of salt, sugar and saturated fats among people of all ages, including children and adolescents. Citing research, the organizers said 97% of people in Bangladesh consume such foods at least once a week.
Speakers said complex nutritional information printed on the back of food packages makes it difficult for many consumers to understand nutritional quality and potential health risks. Clear warning labels on the front of packages could help consumers identify unhealthy products more easily, they added.
The Bangladesh Food Safety Authority (BFSA) has drafted regulations on FOPL, which are awaiting finalization by the Ministry of Food.
Speakers alleged that various food industry stakeholders had been pushing for voluntary labeling instead of a mandatory system, longer implementation timelines, exemptions for small packages and less visible or misleading label designs. They stressed the need for regulations free from food industry interference to protect public health.
Professor Dr Mohammad Shoeb, a member of the BFSA, said the draft regulations were currently with the Ministry of Food.
“The draft regulation is currently with the Ministry of Food. We have already responded to various queries from the World Trade Organization (WTO) through the Ministry of Commerce and are also discussing with business associations on the matter. We hope the regulation will be gazetted soon,” he said.
Dr Mohammad Mushtuq Husain, a public health expert and former chief scientific officer of the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR), said nearly 71% of deaths in Bangladesh were caused by NCDs, with unhealthy diets being a major risk factor.
He said mandatory FOPL could play an important role in addressing diet-related NCDs and called for the draft regulations to be finalized promptly without food industry interference.
Abu Ahmed Shamim, associate scientist at BRAC James P Grant School of Public Health, said warning-based FOPL was the most effective way to help consumers understand the nutritional quality and potential health risks of ultra-processed packaged foods.
Muhammad Ruhul Quddus, Bangladesh country lead at GHAI, said implementing FOPL would help reduce health care expenditure and advance progress toward Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3.4.
M Shamsuddin Ahmed, chief reporter at Daily Ittefaq, said FOPL was an effective public health measure and that the media could play an important role in expediting the finalization of the draft regulations.
Samina Israt, program officer for diet-related risk factors at the World Health Organization (WHO), and Aminul Islam Sujon, a consultant at Vital Strategies, also spoke at the webinar.
The webinar was chaired by ABM Zubair, executive director of PROGGA, and moderated by Mashiat Abedin, a coordinator at the organization. PROGGA Program Officer Shabnam Mostofa delivered the thematic presentation.
Representatives of civil society organizations, nongovernmental organizations, youth groups, the media and various professional sectors attended the webinar.

item.title: Top five Bengali movies to watch this puja
item.description:
Puja is more than pandals and Pushpanjali. It's also about spending time with your family and friends. Whether you are spending time with your family, friends, or alone, movies can be a great start to bringing the festive mood.
Here are five Bengali films, from timeless classics to recent crowd-pleasers.
Poster of `The Elephant God`(1979). Photo: Collected.
Satyajit Ray's Feluda adventure is a Bengali rite of passage. Feluda, Topshe, and Lalmohan Babu travel to the ghats and lanes of Benaras and get tangled in a mystery of hidden treasure and suspicious holy men. It's sharp, witty, and endlessly rewatchable, and the whole family can enjoy it together. Few films capture the "Puja holidays and a good mystery" spirit so well.
Mejbaur Rahman Sumon's first film since Hawa is one of the most talked-about Bangladeshi films of the year. Set in rural Bengal, it follows Shadhu, a poor tenant farmer who keeps trying to leave behind his unpredictable wife, only for her to return each time a palm fruit falls. Part folk tale, part fable, it is shot with a painter's eye and draws on rain-soaked landscapes and old myths. It is darker and slower than the other picks here, so save it for a late-night watch after the Puja rounds are done.
Poster of `Ekannoborti` (1979) . Photo: Collected.
A warm, emotional film about a joint family reuniting around Durga Puja and the traditions that hold them together. Directed by Mainak Bhaumik, it has a strong ensemble cast with Aparna Sen at its heart. It's also a gentle reminder of why we all come home for Puja, so keep tissues nearby.
Poster of `Shuvo Bijoya` (2021). Photo: Collected.
Directed by Rohan Sen, this film is a heartfelt family drama set against the backdrop of Durga Puja. It has the festival's colour, dhak beats, and sindoor khela, along with the bittersweet feeling that comes with Bijoya. It's ideal for watching on or just after Dashami.
Poster of `Utshob` (2025) . Photo: Collected
Bangladeshi comedy-drama film directed by Tanim Noor, loosely inspired by Charles Dickens's classic novella Christmas Carol . A rude, bitter man is visited by three ghosts on Eid eve, learns from his past mistakes, and makes peace with the family and community he pushed away.
So settle in with some Puja sweets and press play. Shubho Sharodiya!

item.title: Walton Hi-Tech holds 20th AGM
item.description:
Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC held its 20th Annual General Meeting (AGM).
At the meeting, shareholders approved a 180% cash dividend and 10% stock dividend for FY26.
At the AGM, shareholders expressed satisfaction with the attractive dividend payout despite persistent challenges in both the global and domestic economic landscape.
They also appreciated Walton’s forward-looking initiatives in lithium-ion battery manufacturing, renewable energy, expansion of solar power capacity and investment in new technology-driven industries.
The AGM was held on Thursday (October 15) through a digital platform, with the participation of a large number of institutional and general shareholders.
Walton Hi-Tech’s chairman SM Shamsul Alam presided over the meeting.
Among others, Walton Hi-Tech’s vice-chairman SM Ashraful Alam, managing director SM Mahbubul Alam, directors SM Nurul Alam Rezvi, SM Rezaul Alam, SM Monjurul Alam Ovee, Tahmina Afrose, Raisa Sigma Hima, Sabiha Jarin Arona, Nishat Tasnim Shuchi, and Shadman Sakib Dipro, independent directors Prof M Sadiqul Islam, Akhter Matin Choudhury, and Johora Bebe; additional managing director (AMD) and chief financial officer Md Ziaul Alam, AMD and head of internal audit and compliance Abu Nafis, the company’s statutory auditor, corporate governance compliance auditor, representatives of regulatory authorities, senior officials of the company and a large number of shareholders also attended the meeting virtually.
The meeting was moderated by Walton Hi-Tech’s deputy managing director and company secretary Md Rafiqul Islam.
Walton Hi-Tech’s chairman SM Shamsul Alam said: “Backed by a strong foundation of corporate governance, we have been able to achieve sound financial results despite various challenges in the global and domestic economies. As part of our continued commitment to protecting shareholders’ interests, the Board of Directors recommended a 180% cash dividend and 10% stock dividend. We will continue working to deliver stronger financial performance and create greater value for our investors in the years ahead.”
Walton Hi-Tech’s managing director SM Mahbubul Alam presented the company’s Annual Report for FY26 and highlighted improvements in key financial indicators, business performance and the company’s future growth plans.
At the AGM, shareholders approved the company’s audited financial statements and audit report for FY26, along with the 180% cash dividend and 10% stock dividend.
The meeting also approved the directors’ report, re-election of directors, reappointment of the managing director, re-appointment of the company’s statutory auditor and corporate governance compliance auditor, and appointment of Johora Bibi as an independent director, along with other agenda items placed before the shareholders.
Shareholders also approved transactions with Walton Hi-Tech’s related party ‘Walton Plaza’ in FY26.

item.title: Savor International unveils 3-day Farm2Food Bangladesh 2026 exhibition
item.description:
Savor International Limited on Thursday inaugurated the three-day international exhibition "Farm2Food Bangladesh 2026" at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB), Kuril, Dhaka.
The exhibition brings together leading local and international companies representing the sectors of agriculture, food processing, packaging, dairy, meat processing, fisheries and aquaculture, cold chain, food safety, smart food manufacturing, and related technologies.
The inauguration ceremony was officially opened by special guests Joris van Bommel, Ambassador, Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, Dhaka, Xie Zhuo, deputy director, Trade Development Bureau, Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China, Eshtiaque Ahmed, senior vice president, Bangladesh Cold Storage Association (BCSA), Kbd Mohammad Masum, president, Bangladesh Seed Association (BSA), Mohd Khorshed Alam, president, Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCCI), Shykh Seraj, media personality and agriculture development, and Md Faizul Alam, managing director of Savor International Limited.
The primary objective of Farm2Food Bangladesh 2026 is to promote the adoption of modern technologies in agriculture and food-based industries, strengthen the food processing and packaging sectors, enhance food safety, expand cold chain infrastructure, and foster international business collaboration.
The exhibition provides an ideal platform for local and international companies to showcase their latest agricultural machinery, food processing technologies, packaging solutions, dairy technologies, meat and seafood processing equipment, cold chain solutions, food safety systems, and smart manufacturing technologies.
Farm2Food Bangladesh 2026 serves as an international B2B business platform, bringing together manufacturers, technology providers, importers, exporters, distributors, investors, and industry decision-makers from Bangladesh and abroad.
The exhibition is expected to facilitate new business partnerships, technology transfer, knowledge exchange, and investment opportunities while contributing to the modernization, productivity, export growth, and sustainable development of Bangladesh's agriculture and food industries.
Postmaster Communication is serving as the Event Partner of the exhibition.

item.title: UNDP signs agreements with 12 organizations for environmental projects
item.description:
The United Nations Development Program (UNDP) signed memoranda of agreement (MoAs) with 12 partner organizations under the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Program (SGP) in Dhaka on Thursday to support community-led environmental conservation and sustainable livelihoods across Bangladesh.
The GEF Small Grants Program, implemented by UNDP, supports civil society and community-based organizations in developing locally driven solutions to environmental challenges while improving livelihoods.
The newly selected projects aim to strengthen community participation, encourage local innovation and create sustainable economic opportunities, particularly for women, youth and vulnerable communities.
Selected through a competitive evaluation process, the 12 projects will be implemented across ecologically significant areas, including the Sundarbans, Cox’s Bazar-Teknaf coastal region, Saint Martin’s Island, Hakaluki Haor, Tanguar Haor, the Chittagong Hill Tracts and the Barind region.
The initiatives will focus on mangrove and wetland restoration, sea turtle conservation, elephant habitat protection, community-based waste management, sustainable agriculture and climate-resilient livelihoods.
Several projects will also introduce circular economy solutions, renewable energy, resource-efficient aquaculture and alternative income-generating opportunities for communities dependent on natural resources.
Speaking at the signing ceremony, Sonali Dayaratne, acting resident representative of UNDP Bangladesh, emphasized the importance of translating the partnerships into lasting environmental and social benefits.
“The real success of these partnerships will be measured by the improvements they bring to ecosystems and to the lives of people who depend on them. Our focus must be on delivering results that communities can sustain long after the projects are completed,” she said.
Earlier, welcoming the participating organizations, Sarder M Asaduzzaman, assistant resident representative of UNDP Bangladesh, highlighted the importance of community ownership and collective responsibility in addressing environmental challenges.
“These agreements mark the beginning of partnerships built on shared responsibility, local innovation and a commitment to sustainable development. By empowering communities to address environmental challenges through locally driven solutions, we can strengthen resilience and create lasting opportunities for women, young people and vulnerable groups,” he said.
The agreements formalize the roles and responsibilities of UNDP and the partner organizations, establishing a framework for implementation, innovation, accountability and sustainable project outcomes.
Particular emphasis was placed on expanding successful community-led solutions and ensuring lasting environmental benefits.
In association with the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, UNDP continues to link biodiversity conservation and climate resilience with inclusive economic development through the GEF Small Grants Program.
The 12 new partnerships aim to demonstrate how locally driven initiatives can contribute to national environmental priorities while improving livelihoods and protecting vulnerable ecosystems across Bangladesh.

item.title: PM attends Abdul Hai’s janaza
item.description:
Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman on Thursday attended the namaz-e-janaza of former Deputy Minister and five-time MP Abdul Hai on the National Parliament premises.
A special munajat was offered seeking the salvation of the departed soul after the janaza held at the South Plaza of the National Parliament in the afternoon.
Tarique Rahman also placed a wreath on Abdul Hai’s coffin to pay his last respects.
Local Government, Rural Development (LGRD) and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Social Welfare, and Women and Children Affairs Minister Abu Zafar Md Zahid Hossain, Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Aazam Khan, Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal, State Minister for LGRD and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, Whip Mia Nuruddin Ahmad Apu and other Members of Parliament attended the janaza.
Abdul Hai, a former president of Munshiganj district BNP and an adviser to the BNP chairman, died at a private hospital in Dhaka around 1:30am on Thursday at the age of 77.
Earlier, the prime minister expressed deep sorrow over the death of Abdul Hai, describing him as a tested leader of street movements for democracy.
In a condolence message, he described his death as an irreparable loss to nationalist politics.
Tarique Rahman prayed for the salvation of the departed soul and expressed deep sympathy to his bereaved family members, relatives, political colleagues and well-wishers.

item.title: Hamza sees red in Sheffield defeat as Wilder questions decision
item.description:
Bangladesh midfielder Hamza Choudhury was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in the first half as Sheffield United suffered a 3–2 defeat to Portsmouth in the Championship on Wednesday.
The controversial second booking came in the 44th minute, leaving Sheffield United to play the remainder of the match with 10 men.
Hamza received his first yellow card in the 35th minute for a foul on Portsmouth winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen.
Nine minutes later, Kavuma-McQueen beat Hamza with a nutmeg, pushing the ball through his legs. Hamza then tripped the Portsmouth winger as he attempted to get past, prompting referee Oliver Langford to show the Bangladesh international a second yellow card and the subsequent red.
Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder was left frustrated by the dismissal and questioned the decision, arguing that Hamza had little room to avoid contact during the second incident.
“Where can Hamza go? I just don’t know where Hamza’s meant to go,” Wilder said after the match.
The Sheffield United boss also claimed that Langford initially appeared to indicate that he would not send off the midfielder before changing his mind and showing the second yellow card.
“I have to be super careful because maybe what I might want to say, I don’t say,” Wilder said, expressing his frustration with the officiating.
Wilder also questioned the standard of refereeing in the Championship and pointed to other decisions he felt had gone against his side, including a late incident involving an alleged shirt pull inside the penalty area.
“There were a number of decisions that incredibly frustrated me,” he said.
The dismissal came shortly after Portsmouth took the lead through Zak Swanson, who fired a spectacular long-range effort into the top corner in the 41st minute.
Adrian Segecic doubled the hosts’ advantage in the 54th minute, but Sheffield United produced a spirited response despite being a man down.
Captain Japhet Tanganga pulled one back in the 59th minute before Tom Cannon headed home an equaliser eight minutes later to revive the visitors’ hopes.
Just as the Blades appeared poised to salvage a point, substitute Ebou Adams struck in the 89th minute to secure Portsmouth’s 3–2 victory.
The defeat denied Sheffield United the chance to record back-to-back wins, while Hamza’s dismissal could prove costly for the Bangladesh international, who faces a suspension that could rule him out of Saturday’s Championship fixture against Bristol City.

item.title: Joty takes positives from Bangladesh ODI tour of Australia
item.description:
Bangladesh captain Nigar Sultana Joty is choosing to focus on the encouraging performances from her side’s first bilateral ODI series in Australia, despite a 3-0 defeat to the hosts.
The visitors’ tour ended with an eight-wicket loss in the third and final ODI at Allan Border Field in Brisbane on Wednesday, 14 October. Bangladesh were bowled out for 172 in 49.5 overs, with half-centuries from Sharmin Akhter and Shorna Akter helping them put up a fight.
Australia chased down the target with ease, reaching 175/2 in just 22.4 overs to complete the clean sweep.
While the results did not go Bangladesh’s way, the series provided several milestones and promising performances for Joty’s side to build on.
The second ODI was a particularly memorable outing for Sobhana Mostary, who recorded the highest individual score by a Bangladesh batter in Women’s ODIs (118) and became the first player from the country to score a century against Australia.
Her innings, combined with a crucial partnership of 195 runs with Joty, helped Bangladesh recover after losing early wickets and post a fighting total. The stand was also the highest partnership for Bangladesh in Women’s ODIs.
Reflecting on the tour, Joty highlighted the contributions from across her squad and the experience her players gained against a formidable opponent.
“Each and every game, one of the players came up for the team, and we have taken a lot of positives from here and will implement them in the future. We will take a lot of learnings from this series,” she said.
The tour also offered opportunities for two young pace bowlers to make their mark at international level. Habiba Islam made her ODI debut in the opening match and finished with Bangladesh’s best bowling figures, taking 2/36 in six overs after dismissing Georgia Voll and Beth Mooney.
Disha Biswas made her first ODI appearance in the series finale and claimed the important wicket of Mooney, who was playing her 100th ODI. Their contributions gave Bangladesh further encouragement as they continue to develop their squad.
Joty was pleased with how the young players responded to the challenge of competing in Australia.
“We have seen a few young players do well. We had two debutants as well. It was challenging for them, but they gave their 100 percent in the middle,” she added.
The experience will be important as Bangladesh look to improve their position in the ICC Women’s Championship. They currently sit eighth in the standings, with one win from six matches, and will be aiming to collect valuable points on their tour of New Zealand.
The ODI leg against the White Ferns begins on 18 December.

item.title: Hope powers West Indies to level T20I series against India
item.description:
A captivating batting display led by skipper Shai Hope guided West Indies to an impressive win to level the five-match T20I series 2-2, setting up an epic conclusion in Bengaluru.
Hope's superb innings of 102* helped the West Indies post 247/3 in Hyderabad and Keemo Paul's five-wicket haul saw India dismissed for just 223 in reply to leave the series tied at 2-2 heading into the fifth game of the series on Saturday.
It was a vastly improved performance from the West Indies, with Paul indicating that the side never lost any of their confidence heading into the contest.
"I think all the guys, we back our skills and we feel we could beat any team on our day," Paul said after the match.
"So it's just about staying calm and believing in ourselves and I think we're doing that really well."
India captain Shreyas Iyer was left to rue a disappointing effort with the ball, with pacer Prince Yadav their only bowler to concede less than 10 runs per over.
"We were unfortunate we couldn't execute our plans in bowling and that's where we fell a bit short," Iyer said.
Having been put in to bat first, the visitors got off to a quick start at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad.
Both the openers, Hope and Jewel Andrew (21), added 52 runs off just 26 deliveries. Axar Patel then removed Andrew, but the dismissal didn't shift the momentum in India's favour.
Hope continued to score at a brisk rate, bringing up his half-century off 28 deliveries, with the West Indies having added 118 runs at the loss of two wickets halfway through their innings.
Shimron Hetmyer (33) and Rovman Powell (24) delivered handy contributions with the bat before Sherfane Rutherford (49) upped the ante alongside Hope.
The duo stitched together an unbeaten 91-run stand for the fourth-wicket stand. Rutherford was able to find four boundaries and three maximums through his innings.
Meanwhile, Hope continued his dream run with the bat, reaching his second hundred in the ongoing T20I series - his fourth overall on the tour (two more in ODIs) - as the West Indies finished their innings at 247/3.
Batting at 90 with just two balls remaining in their quota of 20 overs, Hope smacked consecutive sixes to complete his ton.
India got off to a strong start, putting together 60 runs in the first four overs. Opener Sanju Samson led the charge with a quickfire 56 off 23 deliveries.
However, Keemo Paul found a way back into the game for the Windies, removing both Samson and Ishan Kishan (6) in the fifth over.
Gudakesh Motie also stepped up to ensure India were unable to construct a vital partnership in the middle order, nabbing the wickets of Abhishek Sharma (29) and Naman Dhir (0) in consecutive deliveries.
The onus then fell on Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy to shoulder India to a win.
However, Paul went on to snap three more wickets, making it a second career T20I five-wicket haul as the visitors held their nerve to see out a win and keep the series alive.
Series schedule
First T20I: 6 October, Lucknow, (India won by eight wickets)
Second T20I: 9 October, Ranchi (West Indies won by six wickets)
Third T20I: 11 October, Indore (India won by 14 runs)
Fourth T20I: 14 October, Hyderabad (West Indies won by 24 runs)
Fifth T20I: 17 October, Bengaluru

item.title: Mbappe’s milestone, Mourinho’s reunion, Real’s comeback and ‘shameless’ ban
item.description:
Kylian Mbappe marked his 100th Champions League appearance with a milestone goal, Jose Mourinho received a hero’s welcome on his return to Roma, and Real Madrid produced a sensational late comeback before their coach launched a furious attack on the timing of Vinicius Junior’s four-match suspension.
Wednesday night at the Stadio Olimpico had everything: a landmark achievement, an emotional reunion, a dramatic turnaround and a fresh controversy involving one of world football’s biggest stars.
Madrid looked on course for defeat after Roma raced into a 3-1 lead early in the second half, with Donyell Malen scoring twice in six minutes. But the 15-time European champions struck three times in the final six minutes through Carlos Espi, Endrick and Antonio Rudiger to snatch a remarkable 4-3 victory.
The result gave Madrid six points from their opening two Champions League league-phase matches, while Roma remained on one point. Yet the night’s significance extended well beyond the standings, with Mbappe’s personal milestone and Mourinho’s post-match outburst adding further layers to an extraordinary contest.
Mbappe reaches a century
Madrid endured a difficult opening period as Roma attacked with purpose in front of their home supporters.
Mario Hermoso forced Thibaut Courtois into a fingertip save before Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved lead in the 20th minute, sweeping a superb strike past the Belgian goalkeeper from 25 yards.
Roma nearly doubled their advantage when Malen’s powerful effort slipped beneath Courtois, but the Madrid goalkeeper recovered to prevent the ball from crossing the line.
The visitors, however, needed only one defensive lapse to restore parity.
Hermoso misjudged an interception, allowing Mbappe to race towards goal. The France forward’s deflected effort flew into the roof of the net, bringing Madrid level with their first meaningful chance of the match.
It was a significant moment for the 27-year-old, who became the youngest player to make 100 appearances in the Champions League. His 72nd goal in the competition also moved him into the all-time top five scorers, ahead of Madrid legend Raul Gonzalez.
Mbappe’s milestone came at a crucial moment, halting Roma’s early momentum and giving the visitors a foothold in a match that had threatened to slip away from them.
The equaliser appeared to settle Madrid, with Marc Cucurella and Jude Bellingham coming close to putting the visitors ahead before the interval. But Roma were far from finished.
Mourinho’s emotional reunion
For Mourinho, the occasion carried a personal significance.
The Portuguese coach spent two-and-a-half years in charge of Roma, leading the Italian club to the UEFA Conference League title in 2022 and the Europa League final the following year.
His return to the Stadio Olimpico as Madrid coach was greeted with banners and chants from supporters who had not forgotten his achievements. Roma were playing their first home Champions League match in more than seven years, making the occasion even more memorable.
The warm reception, however, did not soften the hosts’ approach on the pitch.
Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini had insisted before kick-off that his side would stick to their aggressive style regardless of the opposition. His players responded emphatically after the break.
Madrid struggled to respond. Mbappe tested Pierluigi Gollini twice but also had another effort ruled out for offside, while Roma looked increasingly comfortable with their advantage.
For Mourinho, the reunion was threatening to end in disappointment. Instead, his team produced one of the most dramatic finishes of the night.
Three goals, six minutes, one remarkable comeback
Madrid’s revival began with a set-piece and ended with a former Roma defender delivering the decisive blow.
Carlos Espi reacted quickest to a close-range rebound following a header to reduce the deficit. The goal injected fresh belief into the visitors and unsettled a Roma side that had controlled much of the contest.
Just two minutes later, Endrick rose to head home from another corner, drawing Madrid level and turning the atmosphere inside the stadium on its head.
The equaliser set up a frantic finale as Madrid pushed for a winner and Roma struggled to regain their composure.
The decisive moment arrived in the 90th minute. Antonio Rudiger got in front of his marker to guide home from close range, completing an extraordinary turnaround and silencing the home crowd.
‘They do things shamelessly now’
The celebrations were accompanied by anger over the announcement of Vinicius’s four-match suspension, which came just hours before kick-off in Rome.
The Brazilian winger had been sent off during Saturday’s 1-0 La Liga victory over Villarreal after pulling an opponent’s hair. The Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee subsequently imposed a two-match ban for violent conduct and another two matches for protests against the officials.
The suspension rules Vinicius out of several domestic fixtures, including the Clasico against Barcelona on October 25, dealing Madrid a significant blow as they attempt to close a six-point gap on the league leaders.
Mourinho was particularly incensed that the decision became public only a couple of hours before his side’s Champions League match.
“Do you think it’s normal that a player from a Spanish team, who has to play a match that is also important for Spanish football, that two hours before the match a player knows he’s been given a four-match suspension?” he asked.
“Couldn’t they do it now? Couldn’t they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out Vinicius has a four-match suspension?”
The Madrid coach then delivered a pointed criticism of the Spanish authorities.
“They do things shamelessly now. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension.”
Mourinho argued that the timing was disrespectful to both the player and the club, particularly as Madrid were representing Spain in European competition.
“A Spanish team that has earned three points for Spanish football, for the rankings, for the prestige of Spanish football. You want to kill a player two hours before the match; it doesn’t seem normal to me,” he said.
Vinicius nevertheless started against Roma as Madrid mounted their late comeback. But the suspension means Mourinho will have to manage a crucial stretch of the domestic campaign without one of his leading attackers.

item.title: Musk calls on Ukraine’s Zelensky to ‘go’ after satellite slowdown row
item.description:
Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Wednesday for Volodymyr Zelensky to “go” as Ukraine’s leader, after insisting any disruption to the war-torn country’s use of his satellite communications system was the fault of the US government, not his company.
The comments came as Kyiv raised doubts over US support for Ukraine in its war with Russia, accusing Washington this week of helping Moscow by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv’s military response through changes to the SpaceX-designed system it uses for communications.
“And so the slaughter continues,” Musk wrote on X. “Time for Zelensky to go.”
Musk earlier said that “any limits on speed or usage” of his SpaceX company’s Starshield systems were “decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” referring to US President Donald Trump.
He drew a distinction between Starshield, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications, and the parallel Starlink civilian satellite system, which Kyiv also deploys but is not allowed to use for offensive operations.
Musk was responding to a post on X by Ukraine’s former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who said that “Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 km/h is being restored,” but that “removing Starshield’s speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine’s defense.”
Ukrainian defense officials have suggested Washington is behind slower speeds reported on some internet terminals that help the country’s military hit Russian-occupied territory and operate interceptor drones.
Kyiv has also accused the United States of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes, with the city hit by ballistic missiles for two nights in a row before air raid sirens could sound to warn residents to take cover.
A senior official in Kyiv also said that the United States had in recent days threatened to stop providing intelligence about Russian missile launches that Ukraine uses to thwart attacks -- which Trump has denied.
Trump, facing key midterm elections next month in which soaring fuel prices are a major issue, has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for the squeeze on supplies and increase in prices at the pump.
Opposition Democrats in the US Senate and House denounced Trump’s administration over the reported interrupted connections.
“Trump’s making a choice -- and it directly aids Putin’s slaughter of Ukrainian civilians,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats said in a post on X, describing restrictions as “unconscionable” while Ukraine faced an onslaught of Russian drones and missiles.
In the Senate’s Foreign Relations Committee, top Democrat Jeanne Shaheen said the “restrictions on Ukraine’s access to Starshield must stop immediately,” adding that “lives are at stake.”
Shaheen also said that the defense department is required to notify “Congress if it pauses or downgrades intelligence sharing with Ukraine,” and called on Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth to immediately provide that notification if there are changes.

item.title: Bollywood actor Imran Khan asked to leave India after joining protest
item.description:
Bollywood actor Imran Khan has been asked to leave India by October 28 after participating in a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Indian media reported on Thursday.
The Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), a federal government agency responsible for monitoring foreign nationals in India, issued a notice to the actor over his participation in the demonstration, according to reports by The Indian Express and The Times of India.
Khan, 43, is a US citizen who holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card. Indian authorities reportedly consider his participation in the political protest a violation of immigration rules governing foreign nationals.
The actor joined a demonstration at Mumbai's August Kranti Maidan on October 10, organized by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), a Gen Z-led movement demanding electoral reforms and Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in voter lists.
India's opposition parties have accused the Election Commission of manipulating voter rolls in ways they say could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The poll panel has denied the allegations.
Police said Khan participated in the protest despite not being an Indian citizen. A complaint against him was reportedly filed by BJP leader Kirit Somaiya, who accused the actor of being involved in a conspiracy to spread anarchy in the country.
Khan was briefly detained alongside other protesters following the demonstration.
On the same day, the actor posted a photograph on Instagram showing himself inside what appeared to be a police detention van, captioned: “Apparently I'm going for a drive.” The post received more than two million likes, according to media reports.
Speaking to reporters about his participation, Khan said he was attending as an individual rather than representing any organization.
“I don't have demands. I'm here as a citizen, as a person who lives in this city,” he said, adding that he wanted to understand why freedom of movement was being restricted and people's voices suppressed.
Khan has not publicly commented on the notice asking him to leave India, and Reuters reported that he did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The actor, a nephew of Bollywood star Aamir Khan, rose to prominence with the 2008 romantic comedy Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na. He subsequently appeared in films including I Hate Luv Storys, Mere Brother Ki Dulhan and Delhi Belly before stepping away from acting for more than a decade.
He is returning to acting this year with the Netflix film Adhure Hum Adhure Tum, according to media reports.
The notice comes amid growing protests across India over alleged voter-list irregularities and demands for electoral reforms. Thousands of demonstrators marched in Delhi, Mumbai and other cities over the weekend.
On Monday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and other opposition figures led a march towards the Supreme Court in New Delhi, demanding action over the allegations against the Election Commission.
Two senior CJP leaders were also sent to jail for five days on Wednesday after being arrested over alleged trespassing at a protest site in Delhi.
The CJP has called for another demonstration in the capital on Friday evening.

item.title: School roof collapse kills teacher, 32 children in NW Pakistan
item.description:
The roof of a school collapsed in Pakistan’s northwestern city of Peshawar, killing a teacher and 32 students, mostly aged under 14, health officials said on Thursday, as residents and rescuers scrambled to pull children from the rubble.
Twenty more students were taken to hospital after the collapse, which authorities blamed on “weak infrastructure.” Others in the densely populated neighborhood described a close call.
Resident Sohail told AFP “Everyone began screaming in panic” after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse.
“When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said.
Asim Khan of Peshawar’s Lady Reading Hospital said the death toll had risen to 33 by Thursday evening, with most of the victims aged between four and 14.
“A total of 20 injured children were brought to the hospital, most of whom have been discharged. Three severely injured children, who sustained head injuries, have been admitted to the hospital,” Khan said.
The injured and deceased included 12 girls and a female teacher, Khan added.
A spokesman for the emergency rescue service in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way.
“When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside,” spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said.
AFP journalists saw dozens of people at the scene.
Images released by the emergency services showed rescue workers in high-visibility vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.
A senior Peshawar-based official told AFP that initial reports suggested the roof collapse was due to “weak infrastructure.”
“The school owner has been detained,” the official said on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to talk to the media.
Bodies wrapped in white cloth were seen being carried out of the hospital as volunteers arrived to help identify the victims.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed “deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives,” according to a statement.
“The Prime Minister extends his condolences to the bereaved families and prays for them to have the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss,” the statement said.
President Asif Ali Zardari described the roof collapse as a “heartbreaking tragedy.”
Resident Sher Ahmed blamed “substandard construction materials” for the tragedy and called for an investigation.
“With profound grief and sorrow, I urge the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and take strict action against anyone found responsible so that such tragedies can be prevented in the future,” he said.
Roof and building collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and substandard construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.
In June, more than a dozen children were killed when a roof collapsed at a tutoring center in the eastern city of Lahore.
In 2025, 27 people were killed and 10 injured when a five-story building collapsed in the impoverished Lyari area of the southern city of Karachi.

item.title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn from UK retailers over Palestine Action support
item.description:
Irish novelist Sally Rooney’s books will no longer be supplied to retailers in the United Kingdom following her continued support for Palestine Action, which the UK government designated a proscribed terrorist organization in 2025.
Rooney said in a statement to BBC News that publishing contracts for her work in the UK could constitute a “serious criminal offense" because of her stated intention to continue supporting the group with her royalties. She and her publisher, Faber, have agreed to stop supplying her books to UK retailers.
“I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences,” Rooney said.
Faber confirmed that the decision applies to all formats of her books in the UK. Electronic editions have already been removed from sale, while physical copies remain available in some bookstores.
Waterstones told the BBC that Faber had confirmed booksellers could continue selling copies already in stock.
“Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work,” the publisher said in a statement.
“To sell a writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher,” it added, confirming that Rooney’s books would continue to be sold in other territories.
Rooney said she had expressed her intention to continue supporting Palestine Action in an opinion article published in The Irish Times in August 2025. The group is not proscribed in the Republic of Ireland, where she lives.
The UK government proscribed Palestine Action in July 2025, citing its history of criminal damage. The group has targeted arms companies linked to Israel’s war in Gaza.
Rooney’s decision to continue supporting the group also led her to cancel a planned UK visit to receive an award last year because she feared arrest, according to the BBC.
Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori said Rooney had taken “a brave and principled stand” against the group’s proscription. Ammori described the withdrawal of the author’s books as a setback for freedom of expression.
Rooney has sold more than 6 million copies of her novels worldwide, including 2.3 million in the UK, according to NielsenIQ BookData.
Her novels include “Normal People,” “Conversations With Friends,” “Beautiful World, Where Are You” and “Intermezzo.” “Normal People,” published in 2018, was adapted into a television series in 2020, starring Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones.
The withdrawal comes as the UK’s proscription of Palestine Action faces a legal challenge. According to the BBC, more than 3,700 people have been arrested over alleged support for the group, with about 2,500 charged. No cases have gone to trial while the legal challenge proceeds, with a Supreme Court hearing expected next month.

item.title: ‘King’ gears up for teaser launch on Shah Rukh Khan’s birthday
item.description:
Shah Rukh Khan’s upcoming action thriller “King” is reportedly set to unveil its teaser on November 2, the actor’s birthday, ahead of its theatrical release on December 24, 2026.
According to Bollywood Hungama, the teaser is being planned as a birthday gift for Khan’s fans and will mark the launch of the film’s global marketing campaign. The teaser is expected to feature Khan in an action-oriented role with new dialogue and sequences. The makers have yet to officially confirm the reported teaser date.
Directed by Siddharth Anand, “King” marks his second collaboration with Khan after “Pathaan,” which was released in 2023 and became a box-office success.

item.title: Guardian wins double at Bangladesh Fintech Award 2026
item.description:
Guardian Life Insurance Limited has won the ‘Insurance Innovation Award’ at the Fintech Innovation Award 2026 for its Automated Claim Processing System (ACPS), while its Guardian Accidental Care initiative received an Honorable Mention.
The two innovations reflect Guardian’s efforts to transform insurance services through faster, more transparent claims settlement and affordable, easily accessible short-term accident insurance coverage.
Guardian's Automated Claim Processing System (ACPS) has simplified the entire claims journey by integrating submission, verification, assessment, tracking and settlement into a connected digital platform.
The system has significantly accelerated claims processing compared to the previous process, reducing paperwork and manual intervention while enabling customers to track their claims digitally.
Between August 2025 and August 2026, Guardian settled more than 261,000 claims worth over Tk557 crore.
Of these, 43,032 claims were settled on the same day, while 97% were settled within a week, demonstrating the impact of digital innovation on claims settlement efficiency and customer service.
Alongside ACPS, Guardian Accidental Care is making short-term accident insurance more affordable and convenient by integrating coverage directly into event ticketing and registration systems.
Starting from just Tk10, the initiative provides 24-hour accident insurance coverage with up to Tk50,000 in specified health and life benefits, eliminating the need for a separate insurance application process.
Commenting on the achievements, Sheikh Rakibul Karim, chief executive officer of Guardian Life Insurance Limited, said: “Our focus is to make insurance simpler, more accessible and dependable for everyone. Through ACPS, we are improving the claims settlement experience, while Guardian Accidental Care is bringing affordable insurance coverage closer to people's everyday needs. These recognitions encourage us to continue developing innovative solutions that deliver meaningful benefits to our customers and strengthen trust in insurance.”
The dual recognition reflects Guardian's continued commitment to digital innovation, customer-centric services and expanding access to reliable insurance coverage across Bangladesh.

Journalist shot dead in Netrokona
item.description:
In Durgapur upazila of Netrokona, miscreants shot and killed a journalist sitting in a shop at around 8: 15 PM today, Thursday, at Uttarail Bazaar on the Shyamganj-Birishiri road in Kalkamanda Municipality.

The deceased journalist is Lutforzzaman Alif Fakir. He was working as the Netrokona correspondent for the private IPTV (Internet Protocol Television) channel Ruposhi Bangla.

In addition, he ran a Facebook page named ''Detective Article'', where he used to write about various irregularities and crimes.

His family home is in Sunoi village of Pogla union in the Kolmakanda upazila.

Earlier, on 10 November last year, Alif was attacked and injured by assailants with sharp weapons in the Teribazar Ghat area of the Someshwari River in the upazila.

At that time, one of his colleagues who was with him tried to intervene and was also chased away at gunpoint.

According to eyewitnesses and police sources, Lutforzzaman was sitting in a shop at Uttarail Bazaar at 8 PM on Thursday. At that time, two young men came on a motorcycle and fired several shots at him consecutively.

As locals rushed to the scene hearing the gunshots, the assailants fled immediately. Later, Lutforzzaman was taken to the upazila health complex where the on-duty doctor declared him dead.

Officer-in-charge (OC) of Durgapur Police Station, Khandaker Shaker Ahmed Khan, stated that five bullet marks were found on various parts of the journalist's body, including the head, neck, and chest. The matter is being investigated.

Upon receiving news of the journalist's murder by gunshot, Netrokona Superintendent of Police Md Tariqul Islam headed to the scene.

He told Prothom Alo over the phone at 9: 30 PM that it is initially suspected to be a planned murder. Police are conducting operations to arrest those involved.
