item.title: Houthi attack on Yemen presidential palace kills five, injures 16
item.description:
SAUDI-YEMEN/ADEN-BOOMS

The Houthis launched a deadly missile attack Thursday on the presidential palace in the Yemeni government's interim capital of Aden, as Saudi Arabia blamed Iran for the recent dramatic escalation in the long-running war.

The attack hit command centres located inside the Al-Maashiq presidential compound used by government forces and the Saudi-led military coalition that supports them, a Yemeni minister said on condition of anonymity.

Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government it backs have come under sustained Houthi attack of late, shifting the focus of the wider Middle East war that erupted with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

The Iran-backed Houthis have seized swathes of territory along Yemen's Red Sea coastline in recent weeks, and a government counteroffensive with Saudi air support has so far failed to reverse the gains.

Yemeni health minister Qasim Buhaibeh said Thursday's attack left five people dead and 16 injured "among those working to guard the site and civilian employees".

An AFP journalist saw smoke rising and residents of the southern city reported hearing explosions during the attack, the first on the complex since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July.

Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the "cowardly" act on X, calling it a "continuation of its criminal pattern of striking civilian sites and civilians".

Houthis say targeted Saudi oil giant Aramco, vow more attacks

A government minister said on condition of anonymity that Zindani had been present at the time, but "was not harmed in any way".

The minister said the Houthis hit a command centre for Yemeni government forces with three missiles, and another for Saudi-led coalition forces at the complex with two missiles, adding that there were Yemeni and Saudi casualties, without providing a specific toll.

Media affiliated with the Houthis said they had targeted "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them".

Yemen's civil war -- in which Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting the government since 2015 -- reignited after the collapse of a years-long truce, with the Houthis going on to launch their lightning offensive in September.

Riyadh on Thursday accused Iran of encouraging the escalation, saying it continued to arm and train the group.

Saudi Arabia's deputy minister for public diplomacy at the foreign ministry said Riyadh was still in touch with Iran, but that Tehran did not appear ready to make concessions.

"We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," said Rayed Krimly.

The Saudi-led coalition said drones fired by the Houthis at the kingdom's southern region and the city of Khamis Mushait were intercepted.

Yemeni government forces said the Houthis had also fired "several ballistic missiles" at the central city of Marib, which sits in a strategic oil-rich region.

Oman meeting refused

In 2023, regional rivals Iran and Saudi Arabia reached a deal mediated by China to thaw a longstanding freeze in ties, but the latest violence might threaten to upend the entente.

The Saudi ministry official went on to accuse the Houthis of refusing to meet as fighting ramped up between the two sides.

"At the beginning of this escalation, we asked them to meet in Muscat, Oman and they refused," he added.

The ministry later said that the exchange took place in July.

Saudi Arabia suffered its deadliest attack in more than a decade on Saturday when a strike on Riyadh's international airport killed 13 people and wounded around 300 others.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said the group had attacked Riyadh's airport 20 times this month.

Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki said "the Houthis must immediately cease all terrorist operations targeting civilians and civilian facilities, including airports, ports, oil facilities, and infrastructure".

He added the group had "worked to obtain advanced technologies with the help of regional actors", saying they now had "ballistic missiles, attack and suicide drones, and fast explosive-laden boats".

The attacks on Saudi Arabia have tested the country's infrastructure and resilience, the energy minister acknowledged earlier this week.

Riyadh usually hosts a packed calendar of events this time of year, including its flagship investment conference drawing foreign leaders and business titans.

In Yemen, the conflict has caused what the United Nations calls one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, leaving most of the nation's population dependent on aid.

item.title: Man beaten to death in Satkhira after Facebook Live draws a crowd
item.description:
A 38-year-old man, Wahiduzzaman Shamim, was beaten to death in Debhata, Satkhira, after a crowd was mobilised through Facebook Live over allegations of blasphemy. He was beaten repeatedly.

After police rescued him and took him to hospital, he was attacked there as well. He was then dragged outside and beaten again. After his death, a photograph of his body was posted on Facebook.

An analysis of Facebook posts and videos found that Fazlul Haque Ameni, a resident of Parulia village in Debhata upazila, went live twice from his Facebook profile, Fh Ameni, to gather people.

He first went live at 3:31 pm on Tuesday. During the 19-minute-and-19-second broadcast, he played an audio recording.

Fazlul Haque claimed that the recording captured a conversation involving Shamim. Alleging that Shamim had insulted religion, he demanded appropriate punishment and also disclosed Shamim’s home address during the broadcast.

Fazlul Haque went live again at 5:31 pm, this time from outside a village physician’s chamber, where Shamim was receiving treatment. During the six-minute-and-16-second broadcast, he urged people to gather outside the chamber.

He appeared to be inciting those around him as he streamed live. Within a short time, several hundred people had gathered. They then pressured the village physician to hand Shamim over to them.

A video of the beating shows a large crowd surrounding Shamim as he lies on the ground. Several people can be seen striking him while standing on his chest. Another video shows a procession in Debhata upazila town demanding his punishment, with Fazlul Haque at the front.

Shamim, the son of Shamsul Rahman of Subarnabad village in Debhata upazila, was beaten to death in several attacks on Tuesday. His family alleges that a group led by Fazlul Haque killed him.

Facebook posts after the death

Fazlul Haque published two Facebook posts, at 11:11 pm and 12:08 am on Tuesday night. In the first post, he mocked the fact that Shamim had survived the beating. In the second, he confirmed that Shamim had been killed.

Shamim’s younger brother, Tawsif Rahman, told Prothom Alo that his brother had suffered from mental health problems for a long time. At times, he spoke normally; at others, he behaved incoherently. People in the area knew about his illness, Tawseef said.

He alleged that on Tuesday, while his brother was receiving treatment, a group of people known as Jamaat supporters and led by Fazlul Haque assaulted him. Shamim was later taken to the upazila health complex, where the group attacked him again and beat him to death.

Tawseef said his brother had completed both undergraduate and postgraduate studies at Jagannath University. He had also passed the Kamil examination, an advanced qualification in Islamic studies, and studied homeopathy. He leaves behind a wife and two sons.

How the incident began

According to Shamim’s elder brother, Abdul Jalil, an audio recording of a conversation between Shamim and his wife circulated on Facebook on Monday. Someone had recorded the exchange during an argument between the couple.

Allegations that the recording contained remarks insulting religion sparked tension in the area. A group then attacked their home and attempted to damage its doors and walls, the family alleged.

The family said Shamim was first beaten at Subarnabad market, near his home, after the audio spread. He returned home and attempted suicide by drinking poison. He was subsequently taken to the village physician’s chamber for treatment.

On Tuesday afternoon, a group led by Fazlul Haque pulled Shamim out of the chamber and beat him again, the family alleged. Police rescued him and admitted him to Debhata Upazila Health Complex, but he was assaulted there as well.

Md Saiful Islam of Debhata Upazila Health Complex told Prothom Alo that more than 100 people entered the hospital and beat Shamim. They then dragged him outside and attacked him again. Shamim died on the way to Satkhira Medical College Hospital after being rescued from the crowd.

Accused man’s response

Prothom Alo spoke to Fazlul Haque by phone. He said taking the law into one’s own hands and assaulting someone was a crime. However, he claimed that Islamic law prescribed a different response when someone insulted the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said he was dissatisfied with how the authorities had handled similar allegations in the past.

Asked about his political affiliation, Fazlul Haque said he was not associated with any political party. However, he said he took it upon himself to protest whenever anyone made derogatory remarks about religion, the Quran or the Prophet Muhammad. He added that he had led protests over such incidents in different areas.

Fazlul Haque said he had once worked as an imam at a mosque. He now gets called to slaughter livestock at the village market and also transport passengers on motorcycle.

Asked about the killing, Debhata upazila Jamaat secretary Imdadul Haque told Prothom Alo that beating someone to death could never be justified. Anyone facing allegations should have been handed over to the law enforcement authorities, he said.

“It is not right to portray this incident as an organisational activity of Jamaat-Shibir. I condemn Shamim’s beating and killing, and Jamaat does not support this kind of violence,” he said.

Family files case

Debhata Police Station officer-in-charge HM Shaheen spoke to Prothom Alo on Thursday afternoon and evening. He said police were taking Fazlul Haque Amini’s alleged incitement in connection with Shamim’s killing seriously.

Police were reviewing his social media activities and statements, and investigating his conduct, he said. An operation was underway to detain him.

The officer added that police had preserved the videos circulating on Facebook. Investigators were using the footage and technological assistance to identify those involved in the attack and beating.

The officer said the family had been asked to file a complaint over the attack at the hospital.

On Thursday night, Shamim’s elder brother Abdul Jalil filed a case naming 10 people, including Fazlul Haque. Another 200 to 250 unidentified people were also named as accused.

item.title: Durga Puja begins today with Maha Shashthi
item.description:
Sharadiya Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of Bangladesh’s Hindu community, begins today, Friday, with Maha Shashthi. Worship of the main idols begins today. Until Bijoya Dashami next Wednesday, the puja mandaps will resound with the beats of drums and the clang of traditional cymbals over the six-day festival.

The rituals marking the beginning of the day, along with the Shashthi puja, was performed by 9:57 am today. In the evening, the goddess will be formally invited as the rituals of amantran and adhivas will be observed.

This year, Goddess Durga will arrive on horseback and depart by boat. According to Hindu scriptures, the goddess visits her parental home on Earth today, leaving her husband’s home on Mount Kailash.

The gods were once driven from heaven after being defeated by demonic forces. To destroy this evil power, the gods united, and the emergence of a supreme divine force became necessary. Goddess Durga, the destroyer of evil, emerged from the radiance of the gods.

Ahead of Durga Puja, leaders of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad and the Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee held a meeting with journalists on Thursday at the fairground of Dhakeshwari National Temple in the capital.

They said 33,851 Durga Puja celebrations would be held across the country this year, up from 32,351 last year. In Dhaka city, 258 pujas are being organised this year, compared with 261 last year.

This year, Maha Saptami will be observed over two days—Saturday and Sunday. Maha Ashtami falls on Monday, Mahanabami on Tuesday, and Bijoya Dashami and the immersion of the idols on Wednesday. Processions will take place across the country, including in Dhaka, at 3:00 pm on Bijoya Dashami.

Final preparations underway at puja mandaps

During a visit on Thursday, preparations for Durga Puja were seen nearing completion at mandaps across the capital. At Ramna Kali Mandir, the idols had been installed but remained covered with plastic sheets. Decorative lighting had been set up across the temple grounds, along with a gate and a stage.

At Dhakeshwari National Temple, the idols had also been installed in the mandap and covered with white curtains. Final preparations were still underway at the time of the visit around noon.

‘Attacks on idols and temples reported in several districts’

At the meeting with journalists at Dhakeshwari Temple, Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee general secretary Shubhashish Kumar Biswas said in a written statement that attacks on idols and temples during preparations for Durga Puja had been reported in Sylhet, Rajbari, Panchagarh, Netrokona and Tangail.

He added that a historic Kali temple in Faridpur had been burgled. In Sunamganj, homes, shops and temples belonging to members of the Hindu community had been attacked and looted.

There were also reports of a robbery in Naogaon by individuals posing as intelligence agency employees, although law enforcement agencies had responded swiftly and many of the suspects had been arrested.

Shubhashish Kumar Biswas said he did not want to see such attacks during Sharadiya Durga Puja.

BGB, Ansar and VDP deployed

BGB personnel were seen stationed at Dhakeshwari National Temple on Thursday. Lieutenant Colonel Md Mahbub Murshed Rahman, director of operations at BGB headquarters, told the Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS) that around 10,000 Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel would be deployed for Durga Puja this year.

BGB Director General Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui said on Thursday that the force was prepared to take the necessary measures to deal with any untoward situation.

Meanwhile, at a press conference at Ansar and VDP headquarters on Thursday, the force’s director general, Major General Abdul Motaleb Sajjad Mahmud, said 212,818 members of the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party (VDP) had been deployed across the country to help ensure peaceful Durga Puja celebrations.

item.title: Houthi attacks: Passengers travel to Saudi Arabia via 2 alternative routes
item.description:
With flights to Riyadh and Dammam suspended, passengers travelling to Saudi Arabia are having to use Jeddah and Medina as alternative routes. Biman Bangladesh Airlines has extended the suspension of its Riyadh and Dammam flights by one day, until 18 October.

Following deadly attacks by Yemen’s armed Houthi group, all flights at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh have been suspended since last Saturday. The Saudi government then announced the suspension of flights to Dammam from Tuesday.

In a press release issued on Thursday afternoon, Biman Bangladesh Airlines said it would announce its decision on flights to Riyadh and Dammam later. Private carrier US-Bangla Airlines had already announced the cancellation of its Riyadh-bound flights until 21 October.

Biman said passengers could travel to Saudi Arabia and return to Bangladesh via the international airports in Jeddah and Medina in case of emergency. In response to passenger demand, the airline has replaced the Boeing 787 aircraft on its Medina route with Boeing 777s, increasing the number of seats on each flight by 148.

The airline has also arranged three additional flights on the Jeddah route. Passengers have been advised to contact Biman’s ticket sales offices for further information.

Biman said passengers could travel to Saudi Arabia and return to Bangladesh via the international airports in Jeddah and Medina in case of emergency.

Jeddah and Medina the only options

Badrul Islam, a businessman from Lakshmipur Sadar, was booked on a flight to Jeddah scheduled for Thursday 7:30 pm. He is travelling to Saudi Arabia with five family members to perform Umrah. Before boarding, he told Prothom Alo, “The Biman office told us there were no problems with the Jeddah flight. Hopefully, we’ll be able to travel safely.”

Abu Taher, a passenger on Biman’s 7:00 pm flight to Jeddah Thursday, said, “I initially bought a ticket to Riyadh. After the Riyadh flight was cancelled, I am now travelling via Jeddah. I had my ticket changed at the Biman office.” A resident of Muktarpur in Munshiganj, he said this would be his first trip to Saudi Arabia. He will work there at a shop in Riyadh.

Another Riyadh-bound passenger, Tarek Hossain, said he had travelled from Bhaluka in Mymensingh to Biman’s Balaka office near Shahjalal International Airport Thursday morning to get a ticket to Jeddah.

His cousin, Md Hridoy, accompanied him. Md Hridoy is also travelling to Saudi Arabia, but had booked his ticket with US-Bangla Airlines. He told Prothom Alo, “My flight was to Riyadh. That flight has been cancelled. Now I have to change my ticket.”

Outside the Balaka office, another Riyadh-bound passenger, Mokhlesur Rahman, said he was scheduled to fly to Riyadh on a Biman flight at 5:00 pm on the 18th. He had come to exchange his ticket for one to Medina after his flight was cancelled.

During a visit to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Thursday, this correspondent spoke to more than 15 passengers between noon and early evening. Unlike in previous days, passengers whose flights had been cancelled were not seen waiting at the airport. Only those waiting to board flights to Jeddah and Medina were there.

103 Saudi-bound flights from Bangladesh disrupted, affecting 15,779 passengers
According to information provided by the CAAB on Thursday afternoon, a total of 103 flights have been disrupted since last Saturday affecting 15,779 passengers.

103 flights disrupted

According to information provided by the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) on Thursday afternoon, a total of 103 flights have been disrupted since last Saturday. These include direct flights from Dhaka as well as transit flights operating via Saudi Arabia.

Some flights have been suspended, while others have been cancelled, affecting 15,779 passengers. As of 8:00 pm Thursday, when this report was being written, CAAB had not provided any further updates in this regard.

According to CAAB, among direct flights, 17 operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 by US-Bangla Airlines, eight by Saudia and seven by Riyadh Air have been disrupted, bringing the total to 42.

Meanwhile, among transit flights, 22 operated by IndiGo, seven by SalamAir, one by EgyptAir, 14 by Emirates, eight by Qatar Airways, six by flydubai and three by Air India have been disrupted. The total number of affected transit flights is 61.

item.title: Parents lose both sons to dengue within 21 days as deaths continue to mount
item.description:
The couple had two sons: Md Nazmul Hasan Ifti, 24, and Md Intisar Hasan Yas, 16.

Nazmul was a pharmacy student at North South University, while Intisar studied in Class IX at Adamjee Cantonment Public School. Their parents have lost both sons to dengue within 21 days.

Their father is Md Babul Haque and their mother, Nazmin Akter. Speaking to Prothom Alo on Thursday, Nazmin said, “A tiny mosquito has taken away all the happiness from my family. We have nothing left in this world to live for.”

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 331 people died of dengue between 1 January and 15 October this year. Like Babul and Nazmin, many parents have lost their children. Many children have lost their parents, and countless people have lost other loved ones. Many families have also faced financial hardship while trying to save relatives from the disease.

Dengue was first detected in Bangladesh in the 1960s, when it was known as “Dhaka fever”. A fresh outbreak of the disease began in 2000.

The spread of mosquitoes and unplanned urbanisation have turned dengue into an endemic disease in Bangladesh. Successive governments have failed to take effective measures to control it. The current government is making efforts, but deaths continue. In the first 15 days of October alone, 86 people died of the disease. There are also allegations that not all infections and deaths are reflected in official dengue statistics.

Babul and Nazmin lived with their two sons in their own home in Bhashantek, Mirpur, in the capital. Babul retired from the Bangladesh Army as a warrant officer and now works in a civilian position in the army. Nazmin is a homemaker.

Their younger son, Intisar, died on 21 September. Their elder son, Nazmul, died on 12 October.

According to family members, Babul and Intisar contracted dengue at around the same time. After Intisar's physical condition improved, physicians allowed him to return home. However, when his condition deteriorated again, he had to be admitted to Popular Medical College Hospital.

When Intisar died on 21 September, his father was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Dhaka Combined Military Hospital (CMH). Intisar was buried in the family's ancestral home in Panchagarh.

Nazmul was diagnosed with dengue in October. After spending three days at Popular Medical College Hospital, he died on 12 October.

Speaking to Prothom Alo over the phone, Nazmin said, “I was worried about the boys' father. I thought something might happen to him. In the meantime, we lost both our sons. Our younger boy was the tallest among his father and brother. He used to say he was the senior member of the family. And what a senior he was—he was the first to leave us.”

When Babul was admitted to CMH, Nazmul stayed by his father's side. After his younger brother died, Nazmul continued to look after both his parents. Then he, too, died of dengue.

Babul and Nazmin have been married for 26 years. Both are from Panchagarh, where they are now staying at their ancestral home.

When Prothom Alo first contacted Nazmin, she was reluctant to speak. She eventually agreed and spent an hour on the phone talking about her sons and sharing memories of them.

She said the boys were rarely away from her, except when they slept. They would lie beside her, embrace her and talk. When walking, they would hold their mother's hand. Even after they had grown up, Nazmin would still feed them by hand.

Her younger son was an excellent cook, she said. Food he had prepared was still in the refrigerator.

Nazmin said, “We were supposed to go to Panchagarh on 18 October during the Puja holidays. My elder son had booked the tickets himself. Those tickets are still there. Yet, before that date, I had to rush to Panchagarh with the bodies of both my sons. They were supposed to travel to Kolkata with their maternal uncle. Both had obtained passports. But they got the kind of passports and visas that took them out of this world altogether.”

Nazmin had much more to say. Her voice repeatedly grew heavy with grief.

“At the hospital, my elder son would say, ‘How will you live without me?’ Yas is gone too. Just before he was taken into the ICU, my elder son said, ‘Abbu, Ammu, take care of yourselves’,” she said.

Saying that there would be no way for them to be all right again, Nazmin added, “Our whole life is over.”

Babul did not want to speak over the phone. Nazmin said her husband was in a very poor physical and mental state after contracting dengue himself and losing both sons. She might have to return to Dhaka to arrange treatment for him.

Families face financial hardship as well

Alongside the grief of losing loved ones to dengue, many families have been pushed into financial distress.

The treatment of Babul and Nazmin's two sons cost around Tk 900,000.

“I told the doctors not to worry about the cost. Just make my sons well. I would take them home. But I could not take them home,” Nazmin said.

10 deaths in 24 hours

According to the DGHS's dengue report, 10 people died of the disease in the 24 hours from Wednesday to Thursday morning. During the same period, 1,943 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals. Dhaka and Chattogram divisions reported the highest numbers of patients.

The report said 107,259 people had been hospitalised with dengue between 1 January and 15 October this year. Of them, 331 had died.

Bangladesh recorded its highest number of dengue infections and deaths in 2023. That year, according to official figures, 321,179 patients were hospitalised with dengue—more than the total number of cases recorded over the preceding 23 years.

A total of 1,705 people died of dengue in 2023 alone, exceeding the combined death toll of 849 recorded in all previous years.

In 2025, dengue claimed 323 lives. In just over 10 months this year, the death toll has already surpassed last year's total, reaching 331 as of 15 October.

In September, the government launched a three-month special campaign to prevent dengue. The programme aims to raise public awareness, destroy Aedes mosquito breeding sites, intensify cleaning activities and coordinate government, private-sector and community initiatives. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated the campaign on 12 September.

Although the government has emphasised dengue control at the highest levels, questions remain over whether measures are being implemented effectively on the ground.

Public health expert Professor Be-Nazir Ahmed, a former director of the government's Communicable Disease Control (CDC) unit, told Prothom Alo, “I do not see much to be hopeful about in dengue control. The picture is largely one of disappointment. Dengue is no longer confined to Dhaka; it has spread to villages across the country. We do not even understand how Aedes mosquitoes are breeding in rural areas.”

Professor Be-Nazir Ahmed said the current approach to controlling Aedes mosquitoes was fundamentally flawed. Despite efforts using this approach since 2000, dengue had not been brought under control, he said.

“Effective, scientific mosquito control measures are needed across the country,” he added.

Deaths are more than just numbers

Prothom Alo was able to speak to Nazmul and Intisar's parents through their maternal uncle, Roknuzzaman, who was with the family when both boys died.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, Roknuzzaman said people who die of dengue seem to be treated as nothing more than numbers by the government.

“But only those families who lose their loved ones can truly understand this pain,” he said.

item.title: Three children, one teacher killed in Oregon elementary school shooting
item.description:
OREGON-SHOOTING/

Three children and one teacher were shot dead at an elementary school Thursday in the northwestern US state of Oregon, police said, adding that the assailant was a 16-year-old who was killed by an armed bystander.

Another child and a teacher were being treated for critical injuries after the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary school in Bend, a city of about 100,000 people.

Mike Krantz, police chief of Bend, told journalists that the department first learned of an active shooter after a call from a person who reported being shot at multiple times by a person carrying a long gun.

Dozens of emergency calls then reported that a shooter had entered the school and all law enforcement in the area were called to the scene, Krantz said.

Officers arrived at 1:02 pm local time (2002 GMT) within minutes of the calls, said the police chief.

“Moments later, an officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him,” Krantz continued.

“Our officers entered the building and confirmed the suspect was dead.”

Officers performed emergency aid on the victims. The three children who died on the scene were aged five, eight and 11, the police chief said.

One teacher was also pronounced dead.

Krantz said one seven-year-old and one 54-year-old teacher with critical injuries were transported by medics to a local hospital.

He added that the shooter was a resident of Bend.

Krantz stressed that the investigation was in its early stages, but told the press conference it appeared “the shooter had forced their way into the school by shooting at locked doors.”

‘Unthinkable tragedy’

Between 400 and 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary, where more than 40 staff work, a police spokesperson had said earlier.

After a lockdown, Bend-La Pine School District said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.

The district’s superintendent, Steve Cook, tearfully called the day’s events “an unthinkable tragedy.”

“We are heartbroken. We are horrified. This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places, and pray that it never happens here,” he told reporters.

Parents were anxiously waiting at the site near a church, where parent Drew Sharp told CBS News: “I have faith that he’s okay and that he’ll be alright.”

Sharp said his son was a fifth grader, the highest grade in the school, and that children were disembarking from the bus youngest to oldest.

“Which makes sense,” Sharp said, but “it’s just more time waiting.”

Friday classes at schools across the district along with activities and athletic events were canceled, Bend-La Pine said in a statement.

The elementary school is approximately 170 miles (270 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

‘Cannot keep accepting this’

The United States, where firearms are readily available, is a frequent scene of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.

The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.

There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the US so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.

“Our hearts are with the terrified children and the families anxiously waiting to hear that their loved ones are safe,” GIFFORDS, a gun safety organization, said on X.

“We cannot keep accepting this as a fact of life.”

Thursday’s shooting was followed by a painfully familiar chorus of calls for action on gun control, pleas that have resulted in little meaningful change.

In the face of decades of massacres akin to Thursday’s, the powerful US pro-gun lobby has given millions of dollars to primarily conservative politicians in a successful bid to keep gun laws loose.

“They’re killing our babies. Shredding our kids with lead. Forcing us to live in fear,” said Janelle Bynum, an Oregon congresswoman, in a statement.

“This continues to happen,” she said later, speaking on CNN.

“And it seems as if the adults don’t care.”

item.title: Over 20,000 teachers teach English, mathematics despite graduating in other disciplines
item.description:
A total of 9,982 teachers who teach English at secondary schools across the country did not study English at the undergraduate level. The situation is similar in mathematics. Among teachers who teach mathematics, 10,169 did not study the subject at the undergraduate level.

These findings have emerged from the Bangladesh Education Statistics 2025 report published by the Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS). Overall, the report shows that more than 20,000 teachers teach English and mathematics despite having graduated in other subjects.

There are also significant gaps in teachers' professional training, apart from subject-specific qualifications. Nearly 40 per cent of teachers working at the secondary level have no professional training such as a Bachelor of Education (BEd), Master of Education (MEd) or Bachelor of Physical Education (BPEd).

Teachers and academicians said that secondary school teachers are recruited on a subject-specific basis. However, due to a shortage of subject-specific teachers, many schools have to assign teachers of other subjects to take English and mathematics classes as well.

This affects the quality of teaching in schools and leaves students with learning gaps. As a result, many students have to spend additional money on coaching and private tuition outside school to prepare for examinations and pass them.

The BANBEIS report provides data on the number of teachers in government and non-government secondary schools across various subjects, including Bangla, English, mathematics, social science, physical science and biological science. It separately presents the educational qualifications of teachers taking classes in English and mathematics.

Director General of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud Sohel told Prothom Alo that schools face an overall shortage of teachers, not just a shortage of professionally trained ones. Discussions are underway on how to recruit teachers quickly. At the same time, necessary initiatives are being taken with an emphasis on professional training.

Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud said a special initiative has been taken through Khan Academy Bangladesh to improve the standard of mathematics education among secondary school students and enhance teachers' skills. He said there were plans to introduce a system under which people with degrees in education could be recruited as teachers at primary and secondary schools in the future.

Gaps in academic qualifications in English and mathematics

According to the BANBEIS report, 64,253 teachers teach English at the secondary level. Of them, 9,982 hold bachelor's degrees but did not study English at the undergraduate level. In addition, 4,212 teachers have passed the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examination. The remaining nearly 50,000 teachers hold bachelor's, honours or master's degrees with English as a subject.

A total of 67,697 teachers teach mathematics. Of them, 10,169 hold pass bachelor's degrees but did not study mathematics. In other words, mathematics was not among their undergraduate subjects. Nearly 29,000 teachers studied mathematics at the bachelor's or master's level. Among the rest, some teachers did not study mathematics at either the degree or higher secondary level, while others studied it only at the higher secondary level.

A bachelor's degree is the minimum qualification required to become a secondary school teacher. A BANBEIS official told Prothom Alo that some schools recruit a number of teachers on a temporary basis because of an inadequate number of teachers. Some of these teachers have only passed the HSC examination.

Weaknesses in English and mathematics affect examination results

An analysis of students' public examination results also reveals weaknesses in English and mathematics. This year's Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination recorded a pass rate of 64.05 per cent across the nine general education boards, the lowest in 19 years. The number of students achieving GPA-5 also fell by nearly 19,000 compared with the previous year.

The pass rate in English was below 80 per cent in eight of the nine general education boards, with the exception of Cumilla. Results in mathematics were also relatively poor in several boards. As both subjects are compulsory, failures in these subjects affected the overall pass rate.

Weak foundations in English and mathematics at the secondary level also affect students' subsequent academic lives. Even after entering higher education, many students struggle with basic communication in English.

Nearly 40 per cent of teachers lack professional training

According to BANBEIS data, the country has 16,737 secondary schools with 243,557 teachers. Nearly 65 per cent of them have professional qualifications such as a Bachelor of Education (BEd), Master of Education (MEd) or Bachelor of Physical Education (BPEd). This means around 35 per cent of teachers lack such training.

There are more than 25,000 teachers at 2,474 junior secondary schools (Classes VI to VIII). Only 19.52 per cent of them have professional training.

There are also 1,556 school-and-college institutions that offer secondary-level education. More than 35,000 teachers work at the secondary level in these institutions, and 51 per cent of them have professional training.

Overall, nearly 60 per cent of teachers at the secondary level have professional training. This means around 40 per cent lack such training. Nearly 8.64 million students are currently enrolled at the secondary level across the country.

Professor SM Hafizur Rahman of the Institute of Education and Research at the University of Dhaka told Prothom Alo that professional training and certification should be mandatory before teachers join the profession. At present, people may become teachers after completing bachelor's and master's degrees and begin teaching with only a basic understanding of the profession.

However, professional training is essential to develop the competence required for teaching. At the same time, subject-specific teachers must be recruited as soon as possible, he added.

item.title: Emergency rule in Pakhtunkhwa: It won’t be an easy ride for the generals
item.description:
PAKISTAN-POLITICS-PROTEST

The deep political crises in Pakistan has taken  a new turn as the federal government issued a proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule in its  restive province  Pakhtunkhwa on 11 October. Through the said order, the federal government not only removed the Pakistan Tehrik-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government but it has also administratively taken 12 districts of Pakhtunkhwa out of the administrative control of the province and has put them under its own  control.

It is important to remember three things about this  northwestern province of Pakistan: 1. Pakhtunkhwa has been used as a springboard for launching western wars in Afghanistan through Pakistan since 1980  as the “front-line-state”, and the province has  been seriously plagued by terrorism during  the last more than three decades. 2. Pakhtunkhwa is extremely significant for the China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) as the Karakoram Highway that links Pakistan and China passes through the Hazara division of Pakhtunkhwa, and the western route of CPEC passes through the Dera Ismail Khan division of Pakhtunkhwa, linking it to  Gwadar Balochistan. 3. Pakhtunkhwa province  has  been ruled for three consecutive terms since 2013 by Pakistan Tehrik-e-Insaf (PTI),  the party of Imran Khan, the former prime minister and the cricket star of Pakistan, who is imprisoned for the last about three years after conviction in the cases of alleged corruption.

In the general election of 2013 Imran Khan’s party won the majority seats in Pakhtunkhwa with the support of the military’s intelligence agencies who wanted to use PTI as a replacement to Pashtun nationalists in the province. In the general election of 2018  Imran’s party won not only  the Pakhtunkhwa province, but it was  able to win the Punjab province too, leading it to become the ruling party of the country, albeit with the almost naked support of General Qamar Javed Bajwa, the then Chief Of Army Staff.

Actually the generals wanted to get rid of the Muslim League leader Nawaz Sharif who as the prime minister had put the former military dictator General Musharraf on trial before a special tribunal  under charges of high treason for abrogating the Constitution. But in 2022 Imran Khan, who was considered to be the darling of the generals, who were using him for pushing back the “old politicians” for a decade, fell out with the generals on the issue of postings, transfers and promotions in the army,  and Imran was removed through a vote of no confidence by the opposition parties.

Thus he was not able to promote his close ally  General Faiz Hameed to the post of Chief Of Army Staff (COAS) in November 2022, after the retirement of General Qamar Javed Bajwa. In this way, Shahbaz Sharif as the acting prime minister found the opportunity to promote General Asim Munir to the top slot in the Army.

PTI  went for a countrywide protest against the arrest of its leader Imran Khan on 9 May 2023. The military accused them of launching attacks on the military’s facilities and monuments,  leading to a fierce crackdown on the party cadres and leaders. The general election held on 8 February 2024  was again totally rigged in favour of Muslim League (N).

Although Imran Khan’s party was not allowed to win majority in the key province of the Punjab, it was not stopped from winning elections in Pakhtunkhwa province with a two-third majority because the military regards Pashtun and Baloch nationalists as a threat to the unity of the country. But with this development, PTI turned  Pakhtunkhwa as the bastion of the political agitation launched for the release of Imran Khan from prison. Marching on the national capital Islamabad from Peshawar, the provincial capital, with big crowds of people has been the strategy of PTI’s provincial government during the last two and a half years, which has intensified confrontation between the two sides.

However, the picture of political developments would not be complete if one doesn’t note the weakening of the constitutional system and democracy during the last 10 years with the expansion of the military’s de facto control over the state and the government which has led to the dramatic contraction of civilian supremacy.

The military’s control had expanded under the government of Imran Khan ( July 2018-April 2022) as well as under  Shahbaz Sharif’s government (acting government before the general elections of 2024 and the “elected government” after that). The generals have been very uncomfortable with the Constitution after the 18th amendment passed by the parliament in 2010 which has strengthened human rights and federal democracy.

What’s very irritating for the generals is the protection in the 18th amendment provided to the bigger financial share of the provinces in dividing the national financial cake. The generals have been publicly criticising the Constitution after the 18th amendment and they haven’t hidden their intentions for rolling back the 18th amendment. Although the political parties are finding it difficult to publicly commit to rolling back the 18th amendment which was unanimously passed by them, both the ruling  and the opposition parties in the parliament have voted for the 26th and 27th amendments  that have partially rolled back the 18th amendment. Field Marshal Asim Munir’s proposal for smaller provinces is also aimed at curtailing provincial autonomy and strengthening the central control.

But some international factors are also impacting the internal political situation in Pakistan. Field Marshal Asim Munir has  gotten closer to the US Presidential Donald Trump by actively involving Pakistan in  politics of the Middle East. President Trump has publicly admired Pakistan’s role as a member of the Gaza Executive Board and for playing the role of a mediator for stopping the war between US and Iran. Pakistan has also worked very closely with the US for bringing Taliban into power in Kabul and is now  militarily  putting pressure on them to “manage” their strategic orientation.

Every military dictator in the past has enjoyed the support of the US-led Western powers and Field Marshal Munir is not an exception. But in a situation where all the peripheries of Pakistan are boiling and there is almost full-fledged violent conflicts in Balochistan and Pakhtunkhwa provinces, balancing of its relationship with the US and China are becoming extremely difficult for Pakistan. It won’t be an easy ride for the generals.

* Afrasiab Khattak is a former Pakistani Senator and analyst of regional affairs

High prices of essentials continue to squeeze Dhaka consumers
item.description:
Prices of daily essentials remain high in Dhaka despite the arrival of some winter vegetables, leaving low-income households struggling to manage their expenses.
Vegetables are still selling for more than Tk100 per kg in some markets. Although egg prices have fallen slightly, fish and chicken remain expensive. Vendors expect prices of some vegetables to ease as supplies increase in the coming days.
The situation was observed during visits to Dhupkhola, Sutrapur and other markets in the capital on Friday.
Tomatoes were selling at Tk160 per kg, carrots at Tk100-120, long eggplants at Tk80, white round eggplants at Tk100 and black round eggplants at Tk140.
Beans cost Tk120-140 per kg, local cucumbers Tk100, bitter gourds and teasel gourds Tk80, pointed gourds Tk60-80, snake gourds and ridge gourds Tk70-80, and yardlong beans Tk70.
Taro stems were selling at Tk80 per kg, radishes at Tk60, taro roots at Tk70, green chillies at Tk140, papayas at Tk30 and sweet pumpkins at Tk50. Bottle gourds cost Tk60-70 each, ash gourds Tk60 and cauliflowers Tk70-80.
Broiler chicken was selling at Tk180-190 per kg and cock chicken at Tk310-330. A dozen brown eggs cost Tk140-145, while white eggs were priced at Tk130.
Egg seller Nazmul Hossain said prices had dropped by around Tk10 per dozen over the past few days.
“Hopefully, prices will fall further in the coming days. Overall, the market may offer some relief soon,” he said.
Rui was selling at Tk350-600 per kg and katla at Tk300-550. Shrimp cost Tk800-1,600 per kg, pabda cost Tk400-600 and tengra Tk600-1,000. Tilapia was priced at Tk230 per kg and pangas at Tk220.
Vendor Abdul Matin said wholesale supplies had improved slightly, adding that prices could fall as winter vegetables became more widely available. However, transportation costs and additional charges often pushed up retail prices, he said.
Shopper Rafiqullah Rehman said rising living costs had made it increasingly difficult to run a household on a limited income.
“There is no balance between income and expenses. Keeping protein on the plate has become a luxury. Although the prices of one or two vegetables have fallen, there is no overall relief in the market. Broiler chicken, tilapia and pangas are also expensive,” he said.

item.title: Durga Puja begins across Bangladesh
item.description:
The biggest religious festival of the Hindu community, Sharadiya Durga Puja, began on Friday with Maha Shashthi, marking the ceremonial awakening of Goddess Durga.
Temples across the capital welcomed the goddess with incense, traditional lamps, and the rhythmic beats of drums. Rituals, including Bodhan (awakening), Abahan (invocation) and Adhibas (consecration), were performed at puja mandaps.
According to Hindu beliefs, Goddess Durga protects devotees from suffering, obstacles, fear, grief and pain. Religious scholars interpret her name as referring to the divine power that helps people overcome suffering. According to traditional beliefs, the goddess tests people's endurance through hardship and relieves their suffering when they turn to her in devotion.
The goddess is set to arrive on horseback and depart by boat on Bijoya Dashami.
The arrival of the goddess is traditionally heralded on Mahalaya, while Bijoya Dashami marks her farewell. The festival concludes with the Maha Arati, completing the religious rituals.
Celebrations will continue every day from Shashthi to Dashami. Maha Saptami will be observed on Saturday and Sunday, followed by Maha Ashtami on Monday, Maha Navami on Tuesday, and Bijoya Dashami on Wednesday.
Temples and puja mandaps across the country have taken on a festive appearance, with decorated idols and illuminated premises. Devotees welcomed the goddess with conch shells, ululations and drumbeats.
The administration and law enforcement agencies have made extensive preparations to ensure peaceful and uninterrupted celebrations.
A total of 33,851 puja mandaps have been set up across the country this year, around 1,500 more than last year. In Dhaka city, Durga Puja is being celebrated at 258 temples and mandaps.
Government employees are set to enjoy a five-day holiday from October 20 to 24 during the festival.
October 20 will be a holiday for Maha Nabami under an executive order, while October 21, Bijoya Dashami, is a public holiday.

item.title: Four killed in US elementary school shooting
item.description:
Four people, including three children, were killed in a shooting at an elementary school in the northwestern US state of Oregon, US networks reported Thursday, citing unnamed law enforcement sources.
CBS News said at least three children and one adult were killed at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend. CNN also reported a death toll of three children and one adult.
Police earlier told reporters that there were "multiple victims" including children, and that the shooter was also killed.
The shooter was a 16-year-old male, CNN reported, citing multiple law enforcement sources.`

item.title: Coral Future launches operations in Bangladesh to promote decarbonisation, carbon finance
item.description:
Coral Future, a climate change and sustainability consulting firm with 20 years of experience in sustainability and carbon credit solutions, has launched its operations in Bangladesh in partnership with Eelaia and Kayventures to help industries reduce carbon emissions, remain competitive and generate revenue from climate action through carbon finance
The firm helps companies measure their greenhouse gas emissions, develop strategies to reduce them, and implement projects that convert emission reductions into carbon credits and renewable energy certificates.
Its team of engineers, analysts, subject and safeguarding experts works with a global network of project developers, investors, MDBs, governments, end buyers and brokers.
Coral Future operates globally, with a focus on South and Southeast Asia, particularly Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Nepal and India.
The firm's entry into Bangladesh comes as the country targets a 20.31% reduction in emissions below the business-as-usual level by 2035 under its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0, with two-thirds of the target conditional on international support, including carbon finance.
Global brands, export markets and lenders increasingly expect Bangladeshi suppliers to measure and reduce their emissions, creating growing pressure on manufacturers and exporters to adopt decarbonisation measures.
Coral Future offers tailored climate action solutions, including carbon footprinting, greenhouse gas inventories, Scope 3 emissions management across value chains, corporate net-zero strategies, supply-chain emission reductions, carbon credit project development, renewable energy certificates and initiatives to channel climate finance to grassroots communities.
In Bangladesh, the firm has identified textiles and garments, renewable energy, bricks and construction, pharmaceuticals, energy and households, agriculture, and waste management as priority sectors.
In the textiles and garments sector, its focus includes carbon footprint assessments, energy-efficient boilers and machinery, rooftop solar power and emissions reporting to meet global brands' requirements.
In renewable energy, including ground-mounted and rooftop solar projects, it aims to reduce fossil fuel-based electricity consumption, strengthen energy security and lower costs.
For the bricks and construction sector, its priorities include shifting from fired kilns to non-fired blocks and promoting solar-powered plants.
In pharmaceuticals, the focus includes carbon footprint assessments for export markets, energy-efficient cooling systems, improved utility management and solar power.
In the energy and household sectors, the firm focuses on reducing grid losses and gas leaks and promoting clean cooking solutions.
In agriculture, its priorities include water-saving rice cultivation, improved fertiliser use and solar-powered irrigation. In waste management, it focuses on composting and waste-to-energy solutions for cities and industries.
Coral Future also works with project owners and investors to assess carbon credit potential, develop projects, support national authorisation and registration, facilitate verification and issuance, and connect projects with investors and international credit buyers.
Through its two main areas of work — industrial decarbonisation and carbon project development — Coral Future aims to help Bangladeshi businesses reduce emissions and energy costs, meet international requirements, access green finance and develop new revenue opportunities through carbon markets.

item.title: Dhaka air quality turns ‘unhealthy’, ranks 4th among polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka’s air quality turned ‘unhealthy’ on Friday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 181 at 9:20am.
With the score, the capital ranked fourth among the world’s most polluted cities, according to the air quality monitoring platform IQAir.
Singapore topped the list with an AQI score of 236, followed by Indonesia’s Jakarta with 189 and Pakistan’s Lahore with 184.
On Thursday, Dhaka ranked 26th among the world’s most polluted cities, with an AQI score of 105 at 11am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups”, poses health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with an acceptable air quality, while one between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy."
AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI is a daily indicator of air quality, showing how clean or polluted the air is and the possible health effects people may experience.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone.

item.title: 18 railway coaches made in India set to arrive Friday afternoon
item.description:
The first consignment of 18 modern broad-gauge railway coaches, supplied under an agreement between Bangladesh Railway and India’s Rail India Technical and Economic Service (RITES), is scheduled to enter Bangladesh from India through Darshana International Railway Station in Chuadanga on Friday afternoon.
The coaches are expected to reach the Darshana border around 1:30pm before being transported to the Saidpur Railway Workshop after customs formalities are completed.
Mamunur Rashid, station manager of Darshana International Railway Station, said the coaches were manufactured in Punjab's Kapurthala and began their journey to Bangladesh on October 12.
The coaches are currently stationed at Ranaghat Junction Railway Station in West Bengal.
After completing the necessary formalities at Gede in India, the coaches will enter Bangladesh through the Joynagar border point in Darshana, he said.
The consignment comprises 18 coaches, including three air-conditioned sleeper coaches, three air-conditioned chair cars, 11 non-air-conditioned chair cars and one power car.
Upon arrival at the Saidpur Railway Workshop, the coaches will undergo necessary inspections and technical assessments, Mamunur Rashid said, adding that preparations will then be made to integrate them into passenger train services.

item.title: Faridpur Zila Parishad installs 60kW rooftop solar systems
item.description:
Faridpur Zila Parishad has installed rooftop solar power systems with a combined capacity of 60 kilowatts (kW) at two government facilities, with surplus electricity being supplied to the national grid through a net metering system.
The initiative aims to expand renewable energy use in public buildings, reduce electricity costs and promote environmentally sustainable energy solutions.
The systems were inaugurated and a bilateral agreement was signed at 1pm on Thursday, following directives from the Local Government Division.
Under the project, a 40kW solar power system has been installed on the roof of the parishad's engineering department building, while a 20kW system has been set up at the Sadar VIP Dak Bungalow.
Marsh Power Technology Ltd, a company listed with the power distribution authorities, implemented the project. Under the agreement, the company will be responsible for maintaining and repairing the systems for the next 20 years.
A bilateral agreement was also signed between Faridpur Zila Parishad and the Faridpur Sales and Distribution Division of West Zone Power Distribution Company Ltd (WZPDCL-1) to facilitate the supply of solar-generated electricity to the national grid through net metering.
Faridpur Deputy Commissioner Mazharul Islam attended the inauguration as the chief guest. Among others, Zila Parishad Administrator Md Afzal Hossain Khan Palash, Chief Executive Officer Md Bakahid Hossain, Superintendent of Police Shahriar Mohammad Miyazi, Faridpur Sadar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Meshkatul Jannat Rabeya, Executive Officer Sanjida Sultana, Local Government Engineering Department Executive Engineer Mohammad Azharul Islam and WZPDCL-1 Executive Engineer Pranab Chandra Debnath were present.
Speaking at the event, Mazharul Islam stressed the need to expand the use of clean energy to address the adverse effects of climate change and ensure a safe environment for future generations.
“Expanding solar power use across both the public and private sectors can help build an energy-efficient and environmentally friendly Bangladesh,” he said.

item.title: Record 964 Durga Puja pandals in Rangpur, elaborate displays draw crowds in Khulna
item.description:
Durga Puja will be celebrated at a record 964 pandals across Rangpur district and 818 venues in Khulna district this year, with elaborate idol displays drawing crowds and authorities stepping up security to ensure peaceful festivities.
In Rangpur, artisans are putting the finishing touches to idols as organisers decorate pandals ahead of the celebrations. The district will host celebrations at 964 pandals across the city and eight upazilas, the highest number recorded so far.
Of the total, 164 pandals are in Rangpur city’s 33 wards, 10 more than last year, while the remaining 800 are spread across the eight upazilas.
Taraganj has the highest number of pandals among the upazilas, with 165, followed by Mithapukur with 151, Badarganj with 125, Pirganj with 100, Gangachara with 99, Rangpur Sadar with 94, Pirgachha with 91 and Kaunia with 75.
The celebrations will feature devotional music, clothing and prasad distribution, arati competitions and processions marking Bijoya Dashami, said Advocate Prashanta Kumar Roy, general secretary of the Rangpur metropolitan committee of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad.
Rangpur Superintendent of Police Mohammad Mozammel Haque said extensive security measures had been taken, with law enforcement personnel to be deployed before the festival begins. Police have held meetings with puja committees to coordinate security arrangements, while volunteers will assist law enforcement agencies at the pandals.
In Khulna, two temples in Dumuria Upazila have drawn particular attention for their elaborate displays featuring 201 and 152 idols.
The century-old Kharsang Kalibot Tala Sarbojonin Puja Temple in Kharsang village of Rudaghara Union has arranged 201 idols, while the Kharsang Mikshimil Sahapara Sarbojonin Puja Temple, near Mikshimil Bazar less than half a kilometre away, has created 152 idols.
The displays depict episodes from Hindu mythology and religious epics, including scenes from the Ramayana, stories of Lord Krishna, the nine forms of Goddess Durga and other religious figures.
Work on the idols began four months ago. Shimul Das, a sculptor from Satkhira, made 152 idols at the Sahapara temple for Tk3.5 lakh, while Abhilash Mondal created 201 idols at Kharsang for the same amount. Painting work is still underway, but visitors have already begun arriving in large numbers.
School students Tripti Roy, Chaiti Roy and Tapati Chowdhury said they had visited both temples before school to see the displays.
Subrata Sarkar, general secretary of the Kharsang temple, said the two venues had the largest idol displays in the area and were expected to attract substantial crowds. He added that the century-old temple had not received government assistance for its development.
Professor Kartik Chandra Saha, president of the Sahapara temple committee, said the annual celebration had continued peacefully for 52 years with donations from local devotees.
Durga Puja will be celebrated at 225 venues across Dumuria’s 14 unions, said Tutul Kundu, president of the Dumuria Upazila Puja Udjapan Front.
Khulna Superintendent of Police Sardar Omar Faruk said security arrangements had been made at all 818 venues across the district, including 89 designated as particularly important. Uniformed police will be deployed at every venue, alongside members of the Coast Guard, the SRB and plainclothes law enforcement teams. Banners displaying emergency contact numbers will also be placed at the venues.
Authorities in both districts have urged puja committees, law enforcement agencies and people from all communities to work together to ensure peaceful celebrations.
